name: cynergis
summary: The OTO catalog: ontologies and packs, published by Cynergis.

packs.name: agent
packs.summary: An agent people give work to, as a part of a product: the jobs they hand it and the requirement each meets, its tools and what each reads, changes or sends, what it draws on, its guardrails and who confirms, how it talks, where it hands work over, the test conversations that prove each job, and how it is packaged.

pattern.for: a part of a product that people give work to through an agent rather than a screen: the jobs they hand it, its tools and guardrails, how it talks, and the test conversations that prove each job

packs.name: auto-claims
packs.summary: Motor vehicle claims: policy, coverage, claim, incident, handling, money in and out.

packs.name: calm
packs.summary: The FINOS Common Architecture Language Model as an architecture framework for the architecture pack: the adapter that reads a CALM 1.x model into the graph and writes the graph back as CALM, chosen by oto arch import --framework calm, with the migration of a graph written with CALM's former attribute names. The engine ships no framework: this pack installs the first.

packs.name: data
packs.summary: The data semantic layer as facts: a store's tables and columns with their types, keys and a meaning that is a draft until a named person confirms it, the jobs and feeds that load each table (lineage from a dbt manifest or the ETL's SQL), who reads each table and how (usage from the query log). oto data introspect, lineage, usage, meaning and confirm come with the pack, with the data-meaning skill; the engine ships no data layer of its own.

packs.name: ddd
packs.summary: Domain-driven design for the parts of a product that follow it: subdomains, bounded contexts and their map, event storming (events, commands, reactions, read models, external systems) and the tactical model (aggregates, entities, value objects, business rules, domain services), on the architecture pack so a context's deployed component and its framework's node are one node; oto ddd storm reads an event-storming board into a document and a capture the gates take, and a named person signs each element off with oto decide. The engine ships no ddd: this pack is it.

pattern.for: a part of a product designed with domain-driven design: its subdomains, bounded contexts, events and aggregates

packs.name: flow
packs.summary: Executable process graphs: steps with typed executors (script, OCR, Claude, human, terminal), gated by checks against metrics and parameters, connected by guarded transitions with effects, exchanging artifacts with fields; invariants and the tests derived from them. The briefs an agent reads before implementing or testing a step, building the engine, or changing a parameter or an artifact.

packs.name: medallion
packs.summary: Design a medallion data pipeline for a part of a product, source systems to bronze, silver and gold, checkpoint by checkpoint (D1-D9), and the batch flow that runs it, checked by the medallion rules at every capture.

pattern.for: a part of a product that is a medallion data pipeline: its sources, its bronze, silver and gold layers, its rules and the batch flow that runs them

packs.name: organization-process
packs.summary: How an organization works: units, roles, processes, policies, systems and measures.

packs.name: platform
packs.summary: The platform binding of a product's architecture: where each part runs (platforms, accounts, environments with their region, console, logs and provisioning), what it runs on and is built with (managed services, technologies at their versions), its secrets by where they are kept, the pipelines that deploy it, and who decides each choice: a named person, or the builder within limits. Briefs stop an implementing agent that lacks any of it.

binding.for: where each part of the product runs and what it is built with: the cloud and its accounts, environments, services, the stack with versions, secrets and pipelines, and who decides each choice

packs.name: policy
packs.summary: Access policy as facts on the data layer: a rule permits or forbids a permission for the roles and teams it names, a table or a column says how it is classified and whether it holds personal data, a principal holds roles and an agent is granted them; the active rules compile into a signed Cedar bundle, a signed snapshot of what an agent may do for a principal that the engine's guards and write hooks hold a session to, and the platform's IAM bindings derived and never enforced. oto policy compile, snapshot, iam, verify, list and denials come with the pack, with its two build stages and its write and read hooks; the engine ships no policy of its own.

packs.name: portfolio
packs.summary: What we build, who owns it, what we pursue: the products with their stage, domain and value stream, the roles and teams accountable, the objectives of the period and which products pursue them, the capabilities needed and provided, the dependencies between products, and where each product's knowledge base, site and packs are.

packs.name: product
packs.summary: A product's specification and its playbook: Atlas, who carries a product from an idea to a published knowledge base, the PRD captured section by section through the curate gates, and the specification page of the product's studio, read from the graph.

playbook.for: a product, from an idea to a published knowledge base: its specification, its design, its build and its readers

packs.name: product-report
packs.summary: A report product's specification: which report types it must produce, where their data must come from, what layout and fidelity, which channels, which rules and sign-offs, what a run must guarantee, what must stay answerable afterwards, what identifies a document, who owns what, and when a report type is ready.

packs.name: professional-services
packs.summary: Engagements: scope, deliverables, governance, sessions, decisions and the work that follows.

packs.name: report
packs.summary: A report type: its meaning per locale, its sections and fields, the rules that apply, the column that supplies each value, the runs and approvals that produced its template, its operating contract, its lifecycle and the accepted history of its definition.

packs.name: report-medallion
packs.summary: The bridge between a report and the medallion pipeline that feeds it: a report's table is the gold dataset it reads, a column the field behind it, a report check backed by the pipeline rule it relies on.

packs.name: software-architecture
packs.summary: A product's architecture, pattern-neutral: its context and drivers, decisions with their alternatives, systems, components, interfaces, data stores and environments, each traced to the requirement it satisfies; each part handed to the design-pattern pack it follows, found among the project's packs.

packs.name: work
packs.summary: The plan as facts: work items and milestones over the product's requirements, features and components, each open, blocked (on whom, why) or deployed, the state derived from dated transitions and never written on the item; messages beside the item they are about (the communication ontology, on work): a notification from a block to whom it waits on, the inbox a session opens with, replies that lift the block, reminders past a due date. oto work set, board, notify, inbox, reply, event and remind come with the pack; the engine ships no work of its own.

plugins.name: oto-factory
plugins.description: The software factory on an OTO architecture graph: builds a component from the spec the graph projects, with runner, evaluator and aggregator agents, the spec-context skill, a guard and a Stop hook, and the factory-run pack whose code brings the oto factory commands. A use case of the graph in its own repository (ADR-0007). Depends on oto.

plugins.name: pdf-to-template
plugins.description: Turn a sample PDF into a data-driven HTML/CSS + Jinja2 template that renders new data to PDF; the report's definition is read from an OTO project (the report pack). Depends on oto and report.
